newsitem.title: QATAR: France to start delivering Mirages to Qatar in 97.
newsitem.headline: France to start delivering Mirages to Qatar in 97.

text.p: French Defence Minister Charles Millon said on Monday that his country would start delivering 12 Mirage 2000-5 fighter planes to Qatar by the end of the year.
"Preparations are under way and we will start delivering the Mirage 2000-5 planes to Qatar by the end of 1997," he told reporters before leaving Doha after a brief visit.
The two countries had signed the deal in early 1996 to replace Qatar's ageing Mirage fleet which it had bought from France's Dassault Aviation in the 1980s.
"Under the deal Qatar will give its old Mirages to Spain and in return France will supply the new planes to Qatar," Millon said.
He said French airmen would train Qatari airforce pilots to fly the planes.
During his stay Millon met Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani and other senior Qatari officials and discussed ways of deepening military cooperation.

The two countries, which signed a defence treaty after the 1991 Gulf war, have set up a joint military committee to consult on technical matters such as the selection, renewal and maintenance of military equipment.
Diplomats said France was also discussing selling up to 50 LeClerc main battle tanks to the 8,500-strong Qatari army against stiff competition from British and U.S. arms manufacturers.

Millon said France's ties with Qatar were not limited to arms sales. "So many French companies are active in oil, gas and other areas of the economy and we are keen to expand our ties by entering into joint ventures in various fields," he said.
